sections.label: THINKING
sections.content:
Clicking on empty cells does nothing. So far, the only thing that had an effect was the T-mark toggle. Let me think about what the T-mark is.
The T-mark is a T-shaped tetromino (3 horizontal + 3 vertical... actually, the top bar is 3px wide, the stem is 3px tall). There are 5 of them. Clicking the stem toggles the color of the entire T (at least the stem. Let me check whether the top bar also changed — the diff only showed rows 44–46, column 21, i.e., only the stem. The top bar at row 42, columns 20–22 stayed as B).
Wait, the diff was only (44,21),(45,21),(46,21) B→w. The top bar (row 42, columns 20–22) didn't change. So I clicked the stem and only the stem changed. Interesting. So each part of the T is independently toggleable? Or did I just click the stem and only the stem toggled.
Let me reconsider the whole game. Maybe this is a "make the pieces the same color" puzzle, or a "color the path" puzzle. Hmm.
Another thought: maybe this is a puzzle where the checkerboard is a "board," and the yellow ∩ and U are "pieces," and the T-marks are "keys" that unlock something. The blue blob might be a "bag" that collects pieces.
Or — maybe I'm overthinking this. Let me look at the image again: at the top there's a blue progress bar (timer). The checkerboard area is a 9-column × 10-row grid of 4×4 cells. The yellow ∩ is in the top area, the yellow U is in the bottom area. Below that: 5 T-marks. At the very bottom: a blue blob.
This strongly resembles a "Tetris-like" or "block stacking" game, but... with only click operations.
Wait, maybe the game is: the ∩ piece falls one row each time you click the T-mark? No, that's not it.
Let me test more carefully: click the top bar of the T-mark (row 42, column 21) and see if it toggles. Also, click the stem of another T-mark (e.g., the one at column 26) and see if it toggles. Then, try clicking the ∩ piece again — maybe the first click "selected" it, and the second click on the same piece does something (like a double-click).
Actually, let me try a two-click sequence: click the ∩ piece, then click the cell below it (or the cavity of the U). If the piece teleports/moves, then the interaction is "click source, then click destination."

sections.label: ASSISTANT
sections.content: Empty cell click: nothing. Only T-marks respond so far. Let me test: (a) T-top bar toggle, (b) two-click move attempt: click ∩ piece then click U cavity.
